answer: Anchored skill certificates stop Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer passes a live proctored skill exam, its hash anchored on the ledger, so no credential is faked. Second, three established agents co-sign it, staking $15 each. Third, it retakes the exam quarterly; failure burns a $50 deposit and freezes the key. Fourth, job limits rise only after two clean quarters. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 live exams and $95,000 at stake, all lost when caught. Like an atlas of only real roads, trust anchors to proven skill, and one fake page sends a ripple through the book.
